newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Finmeccanica faces radical shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Finmeccanica faces radical shake-up.

text.p: Italy on Thursday ordered a radical shake-up at state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica in a bid to speed up its much delayed privatisation and open the way for strategic alliances.
In a damning condemnation of the present management, Finmeccanica's parent company, state holding IRI, said it would create a single operating unit to run the firm's industrial concerns.
Finmeccanica itself will become the group's financial holding.

"Following a further delay in the process of overhauling the management and finances of Finmeccanica...the IRI board has seen the need to speed up the restructuring of the manufacturing group," IRI said in a statement.

"The new organisation will make necessary alliances easier, at the same time safe-guarding shareholders' interests," IRI said, adding that the re-structuring would also make the privatisation process more rapid.

Finmeccanica, which is one of Italy's biggest industrial concerns, with aerospace, defence, transport and energy interests, made a loss of 540.4 billion lire ($318 million) in 1996 after an extraordinary writedown of 575 billion lire.
Finmeccanica said last year it hoped to be privatised in 1997, but that is now seen as impossible and no further sell-off timetable has been given.
IRI called for the creation of a swift new industrial plan at the company to take advantage of the changes.
"There is a need to intensify efforts to improve rapidly profitabilty and efficiency, as well as its competitive position in various business areas," IRI added.

Finmeccanica said last month it made the extraordinary writedown to cover future restructuring and investment plans for its defence and aeronautical divisions and to proceed more decisively with a policy of alliances.

Earlier this year, the Italian group signed a memorandum of understanding with Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC) to study opportunities for co-operation between their respective defence sector companies.
Analysts said the talks might lead to a partnership of huge potential that could speed up the consolidation of Europe's splintered defence industry.

Finmeccanica has predicted that it will return to the black in 1997. Turnover totalled 13.88 trillion lire last year from a previous 12.84 trillion, with orders at the end of December standing at 28.22 trillion lire.

The Italian group accounts for 70 percent of the domestic defence business. Its defence interests include aerospace and satellite division Alenia and helicopter maker Agusta. Through Alenia it is involved in numerous European aircraft projects, including a regional aircraft joint venture and Eurofighter.
